summary: Iteration 27 — CRITICAL pricing fix verification. The 100x overcharge bug from iter26 is FULLY RESOLVED. Verified end-to-end by (a) calling /api/payments/create-checkout for all 4 packages, (b) navigating Playwright to each returned Stripe URL, and (c) inspecting the displayed amount on checkout.stripe.com. All 4 packages now show the correct EUR price (€997.00 / €4,447.00 / €1,100.00 / €1,188.00 — NOT €99,700 / €444,700 / €110,000 / €118,800). Also verified the /close → close-final-os click flow lands on a Stripe page showing €997.00. Phone validation (min_length=6) works: empty string and '123' both rejected with 422, '+49 151 1234 5678' accepted with 200. 8/8 backend pytest cases pass. Deployment is UNBLOCKED.
critical_code_review_comments: Pricing fix is correctly scoped: only _create_one_time_session (emergentintegrations path) was changed to pass EUR major units. _create_subscription_session still uses int(amount*100) for the native Stripe SDK — that is correct and untouched. Good surgical fix.
Defense-in-depth opportunity: consider also asserting amount range (e.g., 1 <= amount <= 100000) before passing to Stripe, so future plan-config typos can't silently send 99700 EUR or 0.01 EUR.

PLAN_AMOUNT_MAP / PACKAGES duplication observation from iter25/26 still applies but is now mitigated by services/pricing.py being the single source of truth — keep frontend/src/components/pricing/pricingConstants.js in sync via a CI check or unit test.

models.py UserCreate.phone now Field(min_length=6, max_length=30) — solid. Note that whitespace-only strings of 6+ chars would still pass; if that's a concern add a validator with .strip() check (low priority, frontend regex already blocks).

Consider adding a recurring backend test (already added in test_iter27_pricing_fix.py) that asserts each PACKAGES entry produces a Stripe session with the expected EUR amount — would have caught the 100x bug in CI.

context_for_next_testing_agent: PRICING BUG RESOLVED. Verified on actual checkout.stripe.com pages via Playwright cross-domain navigation. The pattern for cross-domain Stripe verification: (1) start on backend origin, (2) POST via page.evaluate fetch, (3) page.goto stripe_url, (4) wait 3-4s for render, (5) read document.body.innerText and regex for €X,XXX.XX. NOTE: after navigating to checkout.stripe.com, any subsequent page.evaluate fetch to backend will be blocked by CSP — return to backend origin before the next API call. Reusable test files: /app/backend/tests/test_iter27_pricing_fix.py (backend), /app/backend/tests/test_iter26_phone_seo.py (SEO/assets).
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (from iter26): emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.CheckoutSessionRequest expects `amount` in MAJOR currency units (EUR, not cents). The library handles cent conversion internally for the underlying Stripe API. Previous code multiplied by 100 (cents-style) which caused a 100x overcharge on the hosted Stripe page (DB stored 997 EUR correctly, but Stripe displayed €99,700.00). FIX APPLIED in /app/backend/routes/payments.py:_create_one_time_session — changed to amount=round(float(charge_amount), 2). VERIFICATION (this iteration): Playwright opened each Stripe checkout URL and read the displayed amount. All 4 packages now show the correct EUR price. The direct Stripe SDK path in _create_subscription_session (line 81, unit_amount=int(amount*100)) was correctly left untouched — that path uses Stripe's native API which DOES require cents. NO REGRESSION.
